holidays.name: National Play-Doh Day
holidays.description: Break out the colorful dough and squish, roll and sculpt your way through the day. It's a celebration of the squishy, salty-smelling modeling compound that has fueled kids' imaginations (and a few grown-up stress-relief sessions) for generations.
holidays.origin: Play-Doh Day was established in 2006 by Hasbro, the toy company that owns the brand, to honor the iconic modeling compound.
holidays.funFact: Play-Doh began life in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner before it was reinvented as a children's toy in the 1950s.

holidays.name: National Guacamole Day
holidays.description: A day to dip, scoop and smash avocados into creamy green perfection. Whether you like yours chunky, spicy, or loaded with lime, today is the day to celebrate the world's most beloved party dip.
holidays.origin: This unofficial food observance is timed to coincide with Mexican Independence Day on September 16. It nods to guacamole's roots in the Aztec sauce ahuacamolli.
holidays.funFact: The name guacamole comes from the Aztec Nahuatl word ahuacamolli, which roughly means avocado sauce.

holidays.name: National Sit With a Stranger Day
holidays.description: Today you're encouraged to step outside your comfort zone. Plop down next to someone you don't know and strike up a conversation, whether it's at a café, on a park bench or in the lunchroom.
holidays.origin: This observance was created in 2020 by BDOPE LLC to encourage kindness, connection and community between people who haven't met.
holidays.funFact: Researchers have found that people consistently enjoy conversations with strangers more than they expect to beforehand.
